title: Thanksgiving Fun & Learning
description: Celebrate Thanksgiving with eight warm autumn activities for preschool and kindergarten: share what you are thankful for, build a turkey, color by number, trace Thanksgiving words, count pictures, finish feather patterns, order pumpkin growth, and search a busy autumn scene.
learningFocus: Say and write what they are thankful for, in words or drawings.
Cut out pieces and build a turkey by following a model.
Recognize numbers 1 to 5 and match each number to a color.
Form lowercase letters on primary handwriting guidelines and match words to pictures.
Count objects by kind in a grid and write each total.
Finish AB, AAB, and ABC repeating patterns.
Put four pumpkin-growing stages in order.
Search a busy scene and count each kind of object.
adultGuidance: Talk first on Pages 1 and 7. Ask the question aloud, let your child answer in words or a drawing, then write, and drawing counts as a full answer on Page 1. Page 2 needs scissors and glue, so stay nearby for cutting, and the small finished turkey in the corner shows where each piece goes. Pages 3 and 6 print best in color. For a black and white print of Page 6, write the color word inside each colored feather first. Pages 5 and 8 both practice counting in two different ways, a tidy grid first and then a busy scene, so encourage your child to mark or point to each picture as they count it. Each page has a short first grade extension. On Page 1, write a full sentence for at least 2 rows, starting with I am thankful for, and read one sentence aloud. On Page 2, count the lobes on the feather fan and write the number on the body, then write the color word for one lobe on its back before gluing. On Page 3, count and write how many sections use each number. On Page 4, after tracing, write each word once from memory on the blank guideline under it. On Page 5, answer two questions under the table: which picture has the most, and how many pumpkins and apples in all. On Page 6, start a new row and make your own ABC pattern with 3 colors, then a partner finishes it. On Page 7, write or dictate one sentence for each stage, and add a fifth box for what happens next, picking the pumpkin. On Page 8, write one addition sentence from the scene, and find which object appears exactly one more time than the apples. The activities line up with common early learning expectations for this age group, including counting and writing numbers to 10 and beyond, recognizing numbers 1 to 5, sorting and counting objects by kind, building shapes and pictures from parts, forming letters on guidelines, retelling a simple sequence in order, and repeating patterns, which are a foundation for later algebra thinking. This is a general alignment note only. It is not an official endorsement by any standards body, and no standards codes appear on the child pages or on the answer key.
